question: Should OpenClaw expose a general internal `session:end` event, or explicitly designate the existing plugin `session_end` lifecycle as the supported automation contract and document its intended coverage?
rationale: The answer determines the public event namespace, payload, delivery timing, and which of reset, cron, webhook, and subagent paths are in scope; that product/API boundary cannot be inferred safely from the open reset-focused PR.

options.title: Adopt internal completion event
options.body: Define and document a typed internal `session:end` contract with explicit lifecycle coverage, then wire every promised completion path with focused tests.

options.title: Standardize plugin lifecycle instead
options.body: Keep completion callbacks plugin-only, define the complete `session_end` coverage and payload contract, and document why internal hooks are not the supported integration seam.

options.title: Limit to reset lifecycle
options.body: Constrain the supported behavior to session replacement/reset events and correct references that imply general completion coverage.

recommendation.title: Adopt internal completion event
recommendation.body: Define and document a typed internal `session:end` contract with explicit lifecycle coverage, then wire every promised completion path with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent internal-hook and session-reset history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-surface contract decision.
